subject: science

concepts.title: Work Done by a Constant Force
concepts.definition: In brief, the measure of energy transfer that occurs when an object is moved over a distance by an outside force applied in the direction of its displacement.
concepts.key_idea: Work is indeed the result of multiplying the force applied and the distance moved in the direction of that force.
question_patterns: calculate the work done when a force of {force} N displaces an object by {displacement} m
how much work is done by a force of {force} N in moving a body through {displacement} m
find the work done if a constant force of {force} N causes a displacement of {displacement} m
what is the work done by a force of {force} N acting on an object displaced by {displacement} m

solution_steps.explain: Work is calculated by multiplying the applied force by the displacement in the direction of the force.

concepts.title: Negative Work Done by a Retarding Force
concepts.definition: Work done when the applied force acts in a direction opposite to the object's displacement, resulting in energy being removed from the object.
concepts.key_idea: Opposing forces like friction or braking do indeed negative work on a moving object.
question_patterns: calculate the work done by a braking force of {force} N that stops a vehicle over a distance of {displacement} m
find the work done by a goalkeeper applying {force} N to stop a ball, moving her hands back by {displacement} m
how much work is done by friction of {force} N opposing a displacement of {displacement} m
what is the work done when a force of {force} N acts opposite to a displacement of {displacement} m

solution_steps.explain: Since the force opposes the displacement, the work done is negative.

concepts.title: Kinetic Energy
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, the form of mechanical energy carried by an object because of its motion, depending on its mass and the second power of its speed.
concepts.key_idea: Kinetic energy scales linearly with mass and quadratically with velocity.
question_patterns: calculate the kinetic energy of an object of mass {mass} kg moving with a velocity of {velocity} m/s
what is the kinetic energy of a {mass} kg ball moving at {velocity} m/s
find the kinetic energy of a vehicle of mass {mass} kg travelling at {velocity} m/s
how much kinetic energy does a {mass} kg projectile have at a speed of {velocity} m/s

solution_steps.explain: The kinetic energy depends on the square of the velocity.

solution_steps.action: multiply half the mass by the squared velocity
solution_steps.explain: Kinetic energy is half of the product of mass and squared velocity.

concepts.title: Gravitational Potential Energy
concepts.definition: The energy stored in an object because of its vertical position or height above a reference level, relative to the gravitational pull of the Earth.
concepts.key_idea: Potential energy is directly proportional to mass, height, and local gravitational acceleration.
question_patterns: calculate the potential energy of an object of mass {mass} kg raised to a height of {height} m
find the gravitational potential energy of a {mass} kg body at a height of {height} m
what is the potential energy of a {mass} kg mass lifted {height} m above the ground
how much potential energy does a {mass} kg object gain when raised by {height} m

solution_steps.explain: Potential energy is the product of mass, acceleration due to gravity, and height.

concepts.title: Conservation of Mechanical Energy in Free Fall
concepts.definition: In brief, the principle stating that the total mechanical energy (sum of kinetic and potential energies) remains constant in a system where only conservative forces act.
concepts.key_idea: In the absence of friction, potential energy at the top is completely converted to kinetic energy at the bottom.
question_patterns: find the velocity of an object of mass {mass} kg at the bottom of a slide of height {height} m
calculate the speed of a freely falling body just before hitting the ground from a height of {height} m
what is the velocity of a child sliding down a frictionless ramp of height {height} m
with what speed does an object hit the ground when dropped from {height} m

solution_steps.explain: Equating potential energy lost to kinetic energy gained gives v^2 = 2 * g * h.
The velocity is the square root of 2 * g * h.

concepts.title: Power as Rate of Doing Work
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, the speed with which work is performed or energy is moved over a given duration of time.
concepts.key_idea: Power measures how quickly work is done, expressed in watts (Joules per second).
question_patterns: calculate the power of an engine that does {work} J of work in {time} s
find the power required to do {work} J of work in {time} seconds
what is the power of a machine performing {work} J of work over {time} s
how much power is developed when {work} J of energy is spent in {time} s

solution_steps.explain: Power is calculated as work done divided by the time taken.

concepts.title: Mechanical Advantage
concepts.definition: The factor by which a simple machine multiplies the input force (effort) to overcome an output force (load).
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, a mechanical advantage greater than one means less effort is needed to lift a heavier load.
question_patterns: calculate the mechanical advantage of a machine that lifts a load of {load} N with an effort of {effort} N
find the mechanical advantage when a {load} N load is overcome by an effort of {effort} N
what is the mechanical advantage if the effort is {effort} N and the load is {load} N
how much mechanical advantage is gained by using {effort} N of effort to move a {load} N load

solution_steps.explain: Mechanical advantage is the ratio of load to effort.

concepts.title: Mechanical Advantage of an Inclined Plane
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the mechanical advantage of a ramp, which is indeed the length's ratio of the incline to its vertical height.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, a longer, gentler slope reduces the force needed to lift an object to a given height.
question_patterns: calculate the mechanical advantage of an inclined plane of length {length} m and height {height} m
find the mechanical advantage of a ramp that is {length} m long and rises to a height of {height} m
what is the mechanical advantage of a slide with length {length} m and height {height} m
how much mechanical advantage does a ramp of length {length} m and height {height} m provide

solution_steps.explain: The mechanical advantage of an inclined plane is the ratio of its length to its height.

concepts.title: Principle of Levers
concepts.definition: The equilibrium condition for a lever where the result of multiplying the both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both effort and the effort arm equals the result of multiplying the load and the load arm.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Increasing the effort arm length reduces the effort force required to balance or lift a load.
question_patterns: calculate the effort required to lift a load of {load} N if the load arm is {load_arm} m and the effort arm is {effort_arm} m
find the effort force needed for a lever with effort arm {effort_arm} m to balance a load of {load} N at a distance of {load_arm} m
what effort is needed to balance a {load} N load when the load arm is {load_arm} m and the effort arm is {effort_arm} m
how much effort must be applied at a distance of {effort_arm} m to lift a {load} N weight placed {load_arm} m from the fulcrum

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the load by the load arm distance.
Divide the load torque by the effort arm to find the required effort.

concepts.title: Mechanical Advantage of a Lever
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, the effort's ratio arm length to the load arm length, representing the force multiplication factor of a lever.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, a lever multiplies force when the effort arm is longer than the load arm.
question_patterns: calculate the mechanical advantage of a lever with an effort arm of {effort_arm} m and a load arm of {load_arm} m
find the mechanical advantage of a lever if the effort arm is {effort_arm} m and the load arm is {load_arm} m
what is the mechanical advantage of a lever when the distance from fulcrum to effort is {effort_arm} m and to load is {load_arm} m
how much mechanical advantage does a lever provide if its effort arm is {effort_arm} m and its load arm is {load_arm} m

solution_steps.action: divide effort arm by load arm
solution_steps.explain: The mechanical advantage of a lever is the ratio of the effort arm to the load arm.

worked_examples.question_pattern: While saving a goal, a goalkeeper's hand moved back by {displacement} m as she stopped a ball while applying a force of {force} N. How much work did the goalkeeper do on the ball in stopping it?

solution_template.explain: Since the force opposes the displacement, the work done is negative.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Calculate the kinetic energy of a cricket ball of mass {mass} kg delivered at a velocity of {velocity} m/s.

solution_template.explain: The kinetic energy depends on the square of the velocity.

solution_template.action: multiply half the mass by the squared velocity
solution_template.explain: Kinetic energy is half of the product of mass and squared velocity.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How much potential energy does a ball of mass {mass} kg have when it reaches a height of {height} m? Assume g = {g} m/s^2.

solution_template.explain: Potential energy is the product of mass, acceleration due to gravity, and height.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A person uses an inclined ramp to raise an object over a step of height {height} m. The ramp has a length of {length} m. What is the mechanical advantage of the ramp?

solution_template.explain: The mechanical advantage of an inclined plane is the ratio of its length to its height.

questions: State whether True or False: (i) Work is said to be done when a force is applied, even if the object does not move. (ii) Lifting a bucket vertically upward results in positive work done on the bucket. (iii) The SI unit for both work and energy is joule (J). (iv) A motionless stretched rubber band has kinetic energy. (v) Energy can change from one form to another.

Fill in the blanks: (i) Work done = ______ * ______ (in the direction of force). (ii) 1 joule of work is done when a force of ______ newton displaces an object by 1 metre in the direction of the force. (iii) The expression for kinetic energy of a body of mass m and velocity v is ______. (iv) The potential energy of an object of mass m at a small height h from the Earth's surface is ______. (v) Power is defined as the ______ at which work is done.

When a ball thrown upwards reaches its highest point, tick which of the following statement(s) are correct? (i) The force acting on the ball is zero. (ii) The acceleration of the ball is zero. (iii) Its kinetic energy is zero. (iv) Its potential energy is maximum.

For each of the following situations, identify the energy transformation that takes place: (i) a truck moving uphill, (ii) unwinding of a watch spring, (iii) photosynthesis in green leaves, (iv) water flowing from a dam, (v) burning of a matchstick, (vi) explosion of a fire cracker, (vii) speaking into a microphone, (viii) a glowing electric bulb, and (ix) a solar panel.

A student is slowly lifted straight up in an elevator from the ground level to the top floor of a building. Later, the same student climbs the staircase, all the way to the top. Given that the height of the building is h = 72.5 m, acceleration due to gravity is g = 10 m s-2, and student's mass is m = 50 kg. (i) Find the gain in the potential energy if the student is lifted straight up to the top. (ii) Find the gain in the potential energy when the student climbs the stairs to the same top. (iii) What do you conclude about the dependence of the potential energy on the path taken?

A crane lifts a mass m to the 10th floor of a building in a certain time. It then raises the same mass to the 20th floor of the same building in double the time. How much more energy and power are required? Assume that the height of all floors is equal.

A man of mass 60 kg rides a scooter of mass 100 kg. He accelerates the scooter to a velocity v. The next day, his son with a mass of 40 kg joins him as a passenger. If the scooter reaches the same speed on both days in the same time interval, what is the ratio of the fuel of the tank used on the two days? Assume that the energy transfer to the scooter happens entirely due to fuel, and no other losses occur due to air resistance and friction.

A ball of mass 2 kg is thrown up with a velocity of 20 m s-1. (i) Identify the sign of the work done by gravity on the ball during its upward motion and its downward motion. (ii) If the ball reaches a height of 19.4 m, how much work was done by air resistance (assume g = 10 m s-2).

The gravitational attraction on the surface of the Moon (lunar surface) is about 1/6th of that on the surface of the Earth. An astronaut can throw a ball up to a height of 8 m from the surface of the Earth. How far up will the ball thrown with the same upward velocity travel from the surface of the Moon?

A coconut of mass 1.5 kg falls from the top of a coconut tree onto the wet sand on a beach. The height of the tree is 10 m. On impact, the coconut comes to rest by making a depression in the sand. (i) Calculate the velocity of the coconut just before it hits the sand. (ii) Assume that the average resistive force of sand is 3000 N and all of the coconut's energy is used to create the depression in the sand. Calculate the depth of the depression the coconut makes in the sand. Assume g = 10 m s-2.
